rationale: Both candidates independently converge on several solid, well-evidenced findings (host/device sync overhead in the packed path, unvalidated max_seqlen_q/k after trimming, the unsubstantiated 'within 2%' latency claim), showing good precision. But the ground-truth's core concern is the AllGather-KV rank-local-Q vs global-KV mismatch in the packed metadata path (P1); Y's treatment reaches the same root cause bobboli described (local Q × gathered KV, proposing a query_ranges-based fix) while X only notes the guard exists and asks for a regression test — shallower engagement. Y also independently surfaces a genuine new edge-case bug (all-false mask silently launching a zero-token kernel) and a SAGE q_block_size gating gap, mirroring the kind of concrete edge-case bug-hunting that produced the ground-truth's P1/P2 findings, and demonstrates verification (ran the CPU test subset, walked through concrete repro inputs). Neither candidate explicitly surfaces the P2 SAGE-silently-disabled-on-exact-alignment scenario. Overall Y shows higher recall on the substantive concern and comparable-to-better precision/actionability.
